quote.text: The Moving Finger writes; and, having writ, / Moves on: nor all thy Piety nor Wit / Shall lure it back to cancel half a Line, / Nor all thy Tears wash out a Word of it.
quote.author: Omar Khayyám, Rubáiyát (Edward FitzGerald trans., 1859)

stories.headline: Nolan Fills the Cinema, and the Theatre Finds a Pulse
stories.dek: The Odyssey opened to the biggest launch of his career and a 95% score; a week later Spider-Man opens here on Thursday to record presales. Two proofs in a fortnight that the big-screen event still pulls a crowd off the sofa.

stories.headline: A Line of Homer, Folded Into a Mummy
stories.dek: A fragment of the Iliad's "Catalogue of Ships" was found placed on the abdomen of a Roman-era Egyptian mummy some 1,600 years ago — the poem, if the reading holds, sent into the afterlife alongside the dead.

stories.headline: Changi Draws Up Its Pre-Terminal-5 Wish List
stories.dek: Ahead of the fifth terminal, the airport has floated six under-served routes it wants flown — while KrisFlyer quietly walls off award searches for near-empty accounts, and Singapore Airlines reshuffles its widebodies for the autumn.

stories.headline: Tehran Says No, and the Barrel Cools
stories.dek: A month into a war that runs through both straits, Iran rejected the Iraqi-brokered ten-day truce on Friday — even as oil, which had touched a hundred dollars on the fear, gave back four per cent, the market pricing the next tanker rather than this one.

stories.headline: Washington Files Singapore Under "Forced Labour"
stories.dek: A new 12.5% US tariff on roughly a third of the island's exports took effect on Friday — the fruit of a forced-labour finding Singapore flatly rejects — even as the chips and medicines that are the real engine were spared. What it does, and does not, cost a household.

stories.kicker: Property · The Quarter in the Books
stories.headline: The Prime End Inverts the Market
stories.dek: URA's final second-quarter numbers landed on Friday, and the usual order flipped: Core Central and landed homes led while the outer rings fell — even as Turf City's first-ever private condo books today, a live test of whether the school belt still pays up.

stories.headline: The Biggest Open Model Yet Lands Monday
stories.dek: Moonshot's Kimi K3 — 2.8 trillion parameters, priced at Western parity rather than under it — opens its weights on 27 July, the closest an open model has come to the frontier. The catch is that "open" now means "if you own a cluster."

stories.headline: Garmin's Answer to Whoop Has No Screen — and No Fee
stories.dek: The CIRQA, on sale this week at US$199, is a screenless recovery-and-sleep band that aims straight at Whoop's business model: all your data in the app, no annual subscription. Whether it undercuts its own launch is the open question.

stories.kicker: The Connected Home · The Weekend House
stories.headline: The House That Knows It's Saturday
stories.dek: Not another gadget this week, but a weekend-morning argument for the local-first setup — where the blinds, the lights and the coffee follow the day with no cloud in the loop — and the cheapest week yet to finish leaving Lutron.

stories.kicker: The Good Life · The Watch Market
stories.headline: The Index Keeps Rising, and Rolex Keeps Slipping
stories.dek: Four straight quarters of gains on the broad watch index — and yet the one name everyone owns is easing at the top. July's read is of a market rising and cooling at once, depending entirely on which watch you happen to hold.

stories.headline: The Rulebook Stopped Counting Hours
stories.dek: America's paediatricians retired the decade-old "limit the hours" advice for a harder set of questions — is the screen any good, is it displacing sleep and movement, can she stop? For a parent of an eleven-year-old, it points the worry somewhere far more useful.

stories.headline: The barrel eases, but the Fed's question stays "hike?"
stories.dek: Oil round-tripped through a hundred dollars and came back — yet a month of it has done the damage: yields ran to fresh highs, the dollar firmed, equities had their worst day in a month, and gold took the crown. The FOMC and the MAS statement both land next week. Market explanation and education, not investment advice; forecasts flagged as forecasts.

stories.headline: The Companion That Deepens the Loneliness
stories.dek: A year-long study across four countries found that turning to an AI companion for comfort predicts not less loneliness but more — the short-term balm and the long-term cost pointing in opposite directions. A quiet preview of the world an eleven-year-old will inherit.

stories.headline: We're Buying Extra Years, and Spending Them Sick
stories.dek: Life expectancy keeps rising; the trouble is that the added years are increasingly lived in poor health. The fix is not a new molecule but the dull, well-evidenced levers — and a warning about the "biological age" number your ring keeps showing you.

stories.headline: The Nearer Nights, and the October Clash
stories.dek: The bookable calendar firms up: Singapore's free late-August Night Festival, a stack of stadium shows into an October squeezed by the first-ever F1 Sprint, and three new tables — two now with verdicts. Book the clashes first.

stories.headline: The Reckoning
stories.dek: On a Saturday this magazine keeps its own accounts. The habit is older than double-entry, older than money — and its history carries a warning: the ledger you try to burn is the one that comes back to collect.
